name: APT32 – APT Threat Map
description: Técnicas de APT32 com cobertura do catálogo (score 3=regra, 2=parcial, 1=lacuna)

techniques.comment: APT32 used GetPassword_x64 to harvest credentials. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used Mimikatz and customized versions of Windows Credential Dumper to harvest credentials. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor can query the Windows Registry to gather system information. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used the `ipconfig /all` command to gather the IP address from the system. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has enumerated DC servers using the command `net group "Domain Controllers" /domain`. The group has also used the `ping` command. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used Net to use Windows' hidden network shares to copy their tools to remote machines for execution. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used the `Invoke-Obfuscation` framework to obfuscate their PowerShell. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor has stored its configuration in a registry key. | cobertura: regra

APT32 has performed code obfuscation, including encoding payloads using Base64 and using a framework called "Dont-Kill-My-Cat (DKMC). APT32 also encrypts the library used for network exfiltration with AES-256 in CBC mode in their macOS backdoor. | cobertura: regra
APT32 includes garbage code to mislead anti-malware software and researchers. | cobertura: regra
APT32 collected the victim's username and executed the `whoami` command on the victim's machine. APT32 executed shellcode to collect the username on the victim's machine. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has disguised a Cobalt Strike beacon as a Flash Installer. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has moved and renamed pubprn.vbs to a .txt file to avoid detection. | cobertura: regra

APT32 has used hidden or non-printing characters to help masquerade service names, such as appending a Unicode no-break space character to a legitimate service name. APT32 has also impersonated the legitimate Flash installer file name "install_flashplayer.exe". | cobertura: regra
APT32 has renamed a NetCat binary to kb-10233.exe to masquerade as a Windows update. APT32 has also renamed a Cobalt Strike beacon payload to install_flashplayers.exe. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor has exfiltrated data using the already opened channel with its C&C server. | cobertura: regra
APT32 performed network scanning on the network to search for open ports, services, OS finger-printing, and other vulnerabilities. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used WMI to deploy their tools on remote machines and to gather information about the Outlook process. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor can exfiltrate data by encoding it in the subdomain field of DNS packets. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used the `netstat -anpo tcp` command to display TCP connections on the victim's machine. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used scheduled tasks to persist on victim systems. | cobertura: regra
APT32 malware has injected a Cobalt Strike beacon into Rundll32.exe. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has abused the PasswordChangeNotify to monitor for and capture account password changes. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used COM scriptlets to download Cobalt Strike beacons. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used PowerShell-based tools, PowerShell one-liners, and shellcode loaders for execution. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used cmd.exe for execution. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used macros, COM scriptlets, and VBS scripts. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used JavaScript for drive-by downloads and C2 communications. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used CVE-2016-7255 to escalate privileges. | cobertura: regra
APT32's macOS backdoor can receive a “delete” command. | cobertura: regra

APT32 has used scheduled task raw XML with a backdated timestamp of June 2, 2016. The group has also set the creation time of the files dropped by the second stage of the exploit to match the creation time of kernel32.dll. Additionally, APT32 has used a random value to modify the timestamp of the file storing the clientID. | cobertura: regra

APT32 has used JavaScript that communicates over HTTP or HTTPS to attacker controlled domains to download additional frameworks. The group has also used downloaded encrypted payloads over HTTP. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used email for C2 via an Office macro. | cobertura: regra
APT32 compromised McAfee ePO to move laterally by distributing malware as a software deployment task. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used legitimate local admin account credentials. | cobertura: regra

APT32 has collected the OS version and computer name from victims. One of the group's backdoors can also query the Windows Registry to gather system information, and another macOS backdoor performs a fingerprint of the machine on its first connection to the C&C server. APT32 executed shellcode to identify the name of the infected host. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor possesses the capability to list files and directories on a machine. | cobertura: regra
APT32 enumerated administrative users using the commands `net localgroup administrators`. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used Dropbox, Amazon S3, and Google Drive to host malicious downloads. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has added JavaScript to victim websites to download additional frameworks that profile and compromise website visitors. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor has modified the Windows Registry to store the backdoor's configuration. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used the `net view` command to show all shares available, including the administrative shares such as `C$` and `ADMIN$`. | cobertura: regra
APT32 have replaced Microsoft Outlook's VbaProject.OTM file to install a backdoor macro for persistence. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has infected victims by tricking them into visiting compromised watering hole websites. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used RTF document that includes an exploit to execute malicious code. (CVE-2017-11882) | cobertura: regra
APT32 has lured targets to download a Cobalt Strike beacon by including a malicious link within spearphishing emails. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has attempted to lure users to execute a malicious dropper delivered via a spearphishing attachment. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used PubPrn.vbs within execution scripts to execute malware, possibly bypassing defenses. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used mshta.exe for code execution. | cobertura: regra

APT32 created a Scheduled Task/Job that used regsvr32.exe to execute a COM scriptlet that dynamically downloaded a backdoor and injected it into memory. The group has also used regsvr32 to run their backdoor. | cobertura: regra
APT32 malware has used rundll32.exe to execute an initial infection process. | cobertura: regra
APT32's macOS backdoor changes the permission of the file it wants to execute to 755. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used Web shells to maintain access to victim websites. | cobertura: regra
APT32 modified Windows Services to ensure PowerShell scripts were loaded on the system. APT32 also creates a Windows service to establish persistence. | cobertura: regra
APT32 established persistence using Registry Run keys, both to execute PowerShell and VBS scripts as well as to execute their backdoor directly. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used pass the hash for lateral movement. | cobertura: regra
APT32 successfully gained remote access by using pass the ticket. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used Outlook Credential Dumper to harvest credentials stored in Windows registry. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor has used LZMA compression and RC4 encryption before exfiltration. | cobertura: regra
APT32's macOS backdoor hides the clientID file via a chflags function. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used the WindowStyle parameter to conceal PowerShell windows. | cobertura: regra
APT32 used NTFS alternate data streams to hide their payloads. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has sent spearphishing emails with a malicious executable disguised as a document or spreadsheet. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has sent spearphishing emails containing malicious links. | cobertura: regra
APT32's backdoor has used Windows services as a way to execute its malicious payload. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has deployed tools after moving laterally using administrative accounts. | cobertura: regra
An APT32 backdoor can use HTTP over a non-standard TCP port (e.g 14146) which is specified in the backdoor configuration. | cobertura: regra

APT32 ran legitimately-signed executables from Symantec and McAfee which load a malicious DLL. The group also side-loads its backdoor by dropping a library and a legitimate, signed executable (AcroTranscoder). | cobertura: regra
APT32 has set up and operated websites to gather information and deliver malware. | cobertura: lacuna
APT32 has set up Dropbox, Amazon S3, and Google Drive to host malicious downloads. | cobertura: lacuna
APT32 has set up Facebook pages in tandem with fake websites. | cobertura: lacuna
APT32 has obtained and used tools such as Mimikatz and Cobalt Strike, and a variety of other open-source tools from GitHub. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has conducted targeted surveillance against activists and bloggers. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has collected e-mail addresses for activists and bloggers in order to target them with spyware. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has used malicious links to direct users to web pages designed to harvest credentials. | cobertura: lacuna
APT32 has hosted malicious payloads in Dropbox, Amazon S3, and Google Drive for use during targeting. | cobertura: regra

APT32 has stood up websites containing numerous articles and content scraped from the Internet to make them appear legitimate, but some of these pages include malicious JavaScript to profile the potential victim or infect them via a fake software update. | cobertura: regra
APT32 has cleared select event log entries. | cobertura: regra
